OpenAI has added support for controlling Apple’s iMessage through ChatGPT on Mac, allowing users to read, write and send messages, search conversations and generate summaries. The feature requires user consent and runs locally on the Mac using AppleScript and Accessibility tools rather than indexing all messages. 
The move comes amid growing tensions between Apple and OpenAI. Apple sued OpenAI last month, accusing it of taking information about upcoming products. The integration could also raise concerns because Apple has long emphasized privacy and tightly controls access to iMessage data. 
Users must grant ChatGPT several permissions, including access to message history, contacts, automation tools and, in some cases, full disk access. The feature also potentially competes with Apple’s upcoming AI-powered Siri, which is expected to analyze messages and other on-device content.

Buffett was late to Apple too. 
 
Even after the iPhone changed the world, he waited years before buying. 
What mattered wasn't the technology — it was the economics. 
Once the numbers confirmed durable cash flow and high returns on capital, he moved. 
Apple became Berkshire's largest holding. 
 
Now the same pattern is showing up with Google. 
 
Berkshire's insurer GEICO was paying Google $10-11 per ad click back in the 2000s. 
Buffett knew the economics of the business for almost 20 years. 
He still didn't buy the stock — and later called it a mistake. 
 
Berkshire finally started buying Alphabet in 2025. 
Q2 2026: the stake jumped 83% in a single quarter. 
#7 holding → #3, behind only Apple and Amex. 
 
He didn't predict Apple's next decade. He waited for the numbers to confirm the business. 
 
Same question now with Alphabet: 
Can it do what Apple did?
